name: Agenesis of the Superior Vena Cava

criteria.description: Imaging evidence of complete absence of the superior vena cava
Presence of collateral venous pathways compensating for absent superior vena cava
Symptoms or signs related to venous congestion or upper body venous hypertension

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of superior vena cava absence with evidence of collateral circulation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on advanced imaging modalities such as CT or MRI venography.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absence of superior vena cava on imaging
searchTerms: missing large chest vein on scan

pathognomonic.symptomName: Prominent collateral venous circulation in upper thorax
pathognomonic.notes: Compensatory venous pathways visible on imaging
searchTerms: visible alternative veins in upper chest

common.notes: May cause facial and neck swelling
searchTerms: swelling from upper body vein backup

common.notes: Visible distension due to impaired venous return
Secondary to venous congestion or associated cardiac anomalies

occasional.notes: Resulting from impaired cerebral venous drainage
searchTerms: head pain due to venous congestion

occasional.notes: Possibly due to compromised cerebral circulation
Non-specific symptom related to venous congestion
May be associated with arrhythmias secondary to altered hemodynamics

rare.notes: Due to impaired venous return and hypoxia
searchTerms: poor oxygen in arms causing blue skin

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits from cerebral venous congestion
rare.notes: Rare complications include seizures or focal deficits
searchTerms: neurological problems due to brain vein congestion
nerve deficits from cerebral vein pressure

laboratory: Possible mild hypoxemia on arterial blood gas if severe venous congestion
imaging: Absence of superior vena cava on CT or MRI venography
Prominent collateral venous pathways (e.g., azygos, hemiazygos veins)
Echocardiography may show associated cardiac anomalies or venous flow abnormalities
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be sporadic or associated with congenital syndromes
other: Venous pressure measurements may show elevated upper body venous pressures
Venography confirms absence and collateral circulation

distinguishingFeatures: Usually caused by external compression or thrombosis
Presence of underlying malignancy or thrombosis on imaging
Presence of an additional left-sided superior vena cava
Superior vena cava is present but duplicated

redFlags: Severe upper body venous congestion with airway compromise
Neurological deficits suggestive of cerebral venous hypertension
Signs of cardiac failure or severe hemodynamic compromise
references: Bergman RA, et al. Illustrated Encyclopedia of Human Anatomic Variation. 2016.
Shah SS, et al. Congenital absence of the superior vena cava: case report and review. Pediatr Cardiol. 2018.
Orphanet: Agenesis of the superior vena cava (ORPHA:99114)
